title: Sikka's Mystery Coin: A Money Story for Kids (Episode 2)
content:
Sikka finds a shiny coin under the sofa. It is silver, with a star on it. It looks very different from Sikka!

The story

Should Sikka keep it? No! When you find money, always tell a grown-up first. So Piggu and Sikka show it to Grandma.

Grandma smiles. "This coin is from my trip to a faraway country!" Different countries use different money. Coins can have different shapes, colours and pictures.

Grandma gives Piggu 5 travel coins for Piggu's coin collection.

Pause and guess! 🤔

Piggu's coin collection has 20 coins. Grandma adds 5 more. How many coins are in the collection now?

Answer: 25 coins! 20 + 5 = 25.

Today's lesson ⭐

Different countries use different money! 🌍

Try it at home

Ask a grown-up if you can look at some coins together. Draw two coins: one you know, and one you imagine from a faraway land. What picture would your coin have?

title: The Lemonade Stand: A Money Story for Kids (Episode 3)
content:
Piggu wants to earn some coins. "How can I do it?" asks Piggu.

The story

Sikka has an idea: "Let's make a lemonade stand!" The lemons cost 10 coins. Each cup of lemonade sells for 5 coins.

Piggu squeezes the lemons, stirs the lemonade and serves happy friends. That is hard work!

Pause and guess! 🤔

Piggu sells 6 cups. Each cup is 5 coins. How many coins does Piggu get?

Answer: 30 coins! Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30.

But wait! The lemons cost 10 coins. So Piggu keeps 30 − 10 = 20 coins. That is what Piggu really earned.

Today's lesson ⭐

Work hard, earn coins! 💪

Try it at home

Play shop at home! Make price tags of 5 coins for toy cups. Sell 4 cups to a grown-up. How many coins did you get? (4 × 5 = 20)

title: The Need or Want Market: A Money Story for Kids (Episode 4)
content:
Piggu and Sikka go to the market. Piggu wants EVERYTHING!

The story

Sikka says, "First, buy what you NEED." A need is something we must have, like food and water. A want is nice to have, like a toy or a sticker.

Let's sort: an apple is a need. Water is a need. A toy car is a want. A sticker is a want.

Pause and guess! 🤔

Piggu has 20 coins. An apple costs 10 coins and a toy car costs 20 coins. What should Piggu buy first?

Answer: the apple! Needs come first. Piggu still has 10 coins left, and can save up for the toy car later.

Today's lesson ⭐

Needs first, wants later! 🍎

Try it at home

Draw two boxes on paper: NEED and WANT. Draw 3 things in each box. Ask a grown-up which needs your family buys every week.

title: Sikka's Three Magic Jars: A Money Story for Kids (Episode 5)
content:
Sikka has a great idea: three magic jars! One says SAVE, one says SPEND and one says SHARE.

The story

The SAVE jar is for big dreams. The SPEND jar is for small treats. The SHARE jar is for helping others.

Piggu has 30 coins. How should Piggu put them in the jars?

Pause and guess! 🤔

Piggu puts the same number of coins in each of the 3 jars. How many coins go in each jar?

Answer: 10 coins in each jar! 10 + 10 + 10 = 30.

Then a friend's pencil breaks. Which jar should Piggu use? The SHARE jar! Sharing makes friends happy.

Today's lesson ⭐

Save, spend and share! ✨

Try it at home

Make your own three jars from cups or boxes. Write SAVE, SPEND and SHARE on them. Decorate them with crayons!

title: The Price Tag Puzzle: A Money Story for Kids (Episode 6)
content:
Piggu wants a new ball. At Shop A, the ball costs 40 coins.

The story

Sikka says, "Let's compare before we buy!" At Shop B, the SAME ball costs only 25 coins!

Pause and guess! 🤔

The ball is 40 coins at Shop A and 25 coins at Shop B. How many coins does Piggu save by buying at Shop B?

Answer: 15 coins! 40 − 25 = 15.

Then Shop C shows a big sign: "SALE! Only 30 coins!" Is 30 cheaper than 25? No! A big SALE sign does not always mean the lowest price. Always compare the numbers.

Today's lesson ⭐

Compare prices before you buy! 🔍

Try it at home

Next time you go shopping with a grown-up, find one thing and look at two prices for it. Which one is less?

title: A Gift for Grandma: A Money Story for Kids (Episode 7)
content:
Grandma's birthday is coming soon! Piggu wants to give her a cosy scarf. It costs 30 coins.

The story

Piggu decides to save 5 coins every day.

Pause and guess! 🤔

Piggu saves 5 coins a day. How many days to get 30 coins?

Answer: 6 days! Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30.

On Day 4, Piggu sees a toy robot for 15 coins. Buy it or keep saving? Keep saving! Grandma's gift comes first. Piggu also makes a birthday card with love. Grandma is so happy!

Today's lesson ⭐

Saving for others feels great! 💝

Try it at home

Make a birthday card for someone you love. Gifts do not have to cost coins: a card, a drawing or a hug is a gift too!

title: The Wait-a-Day Rule: A Money Story for Kids (Episode 8)
content:
Piggu sees a toy and shouts, "I MUST have it right now!" The toy costs 25 coins. Piggu has 30 coins.

The story

Sikka says, "Try the Wait-a-Day Rule! Wait one day before you buy."

Pause and guess! 🤔

The toy costs 25 coins. Piggu has 30 coins. If Piggu buys it, how many coins are left?

Answer: only 5 coins. 30 − 25 = 5.

The next day, Piggu does not want the toy anymore! Piggu still has all 30 coins. Waiting helped Piggu choose better.

Today's lesson ⭐

Wait a day before you buy! ⏰

Try it at home

Next time you really want something, write it on a paper and wait one day. The next day, ask yourself: do I still want it?

title: The Coin Count Race: A Money Story for Kids (Episode 9)
content:
It's the Coin Count Race! Each stack has 5 coins.

The story

Counting one by one is slow. Counting by 5s is super fast: 5, 10, 15, 20…

Pause and guess! 🤔

There are 10 stacks of 5 coins. What is the total?

Answer: 50 coins! 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50.

Then Sikka adds 1 more stack of 5. Now the total is 55 coins (50 + 5 = 55).

Today's lesson ⭐

Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15… 🏁

Try it at home

Make piles of 5 with buttons, beads or pebbles. Count them by 5s with a grown-up. How fast can you go?
